intent: Stop the admission-parity bridge turning a CANCELLED dependency into a verdict on a REQUIRED context, in EITHER direction. Observed twice on 2026-08-07: pr-ci-health supersedes a run whose session-status has starved in the queue, the bridge still runs under always(), and `test cancelled = success` reports hard failure. While the queue starves session-status, no PR can earn a green parity check. The fix is `!cancelled()`: a real FAILURE still runs the bridge and blocks (overriding the implicit needs-success gate), and a CANCELLATION cancels the bridge rather than skipping it. Skipping would be worse than the original bug — SKIPPED counts as a pass in branch protection and in scripts/runtime/pr_merge_control.py:53, and an operator-initiated cancel has no successor run, so the gate would go green with the onboarding evidence never gathered.

commit.message: fix(ci): admission-parity bridge must not read cancelled as failed

interface_mismatches: The bridge's condition decides whether it runs; its body decides pass/fail. A cancelled dependency was reaching the body, where the only vocabulary is success/not-success, so an infrastructure event became a verdict.
honest_blockers: CEREMONY ORDER WAS VIOLATED AND THIS RECEIPT SAYS SO: the fix and its tests were authored before this packet existed. Read the binding as scope CONFORMANCE, not scope-declared-first.

I SHIPPED A FALSE-GREEN ON A REQUIRED SAFETY GATE AND REVIEW CAUGHT IT, NOT ME. The first version of this fix skipped the bridge on cancellation (`always() && result != 'cancelled'`). A SKIPPED required check counts as a PASS (scripts/runtime/pr_merge_control.py:53, PASS_CONCLUSIONS = SUCCESS, SKIPPED, NEUTRAL), and `Onboarding session status` is not itself required, so nothing else covered the gap. The reasoning error was assuming a cancellation implies a successor run for the same head; an operator clicking "Cancel workflow" breaks that invariant. I had recorded this exact risk in this file's own honest_blockers and shipped anyway — a written blocker is not a control. Corrected to `!cancelled()`, which cancels the job instead; CANCELLED is in BAD_CONCLUSIONS and blocks.

I SATISFIED A GATE WITH MY OWN COMMENT PROSE — the exact CLAUDE.md hard rule "never add prose to satisfy a gate", committed accidentally, and caught by Devin, not by me. tests/test_onboarding_ci_contract.py:_job_block() returned raw job text INCLUDING comments, and every assertion in that file is a substring test over it. When I replaced `always()` with `!cancelled()`, the 24-line comment I wrote to explain the replacement contained the literal string `always()` twice, so `assert "always()" in compat` stayed green while asserting nothing about the condition. My own earlier test run reported this file as passing and I read that as evidence. Fixed at the class level, not the instance: _job_block() now strips comment-only lines, so no `in` assertion in that file can be satisfied by prose and no `not in` assertion can be broken by it; the condition assertion additionally reads the parsed YAML `if` value. One caller that deliberately asserts a comment leads the steps list uses an explicit _job_block_with_comments(). Negative control 'condition-reverted-while-prose-still-claims-the-fix-is-caught' reproduces the original bypass and proves it now fails.

Verified by contract tests over the workflow YAML and two negative controls, NOT by observing a real superseded run go green, nor by observing a real operator cancel block. The proof that it works is the next cancellation, which I cannot schedule.

Does not address the cause: the queue depth that starves session-status for 90 minutes. The pr-ci-health merge-to-main rebase trigger that drove that depth was removed separately (#1289, merged). This only stops the symptom being mislabelled.
session_entry.rollback: Single revert. The bridge returns to reporting cancelled dependencies as failures.
